info.title: Life Links Application HTTP API
info.description: Published v1 contract for the implemented Life Links HTTP surface. It covers operational release identity, web application and retained bearer API workflows, the canonical owner reads and revision-safe writes reused by page-bound WebMCP tools, and the stable QR browser entry point. Generic SPA fallback routes remain implementation details outside this contract.

post.summary: Receive authenticated Microsoft Calendar synchronization hints
post.description: Exact public webhook, registered before owner session and browser Origin guards. Subscription validation echoes a bounded opaque validationToken as text/plain. Notifications require the exact stored subscription key and constant-time matching clientState hash on a live owned connection. Invalid or unrelated notifications are ignored. Accepted notifications only coalesce synchronization hints; they never write event truth or grant access. Provider delta/readback remains authoritative.

parameters.name: subscriptionKey
parameters.description: Required for notification admission, not for validation echo.

200.description: Bounded validation-token echo.

202.description: Accepted or safely ignored notification batch.

post.summary: Start owner-session-bound Microsoft Calendar OAuth
post.description: Human owner only; agent-tagged requests are refused. Existing session, browser-origin and rate-limit boundaries apply. Provider credentials and PKCE material remain server-private. Authorization Code with PKCE S256 and one-use state is bound to the exact initiating authenticated session. Reconnect retains the exact owned provider account. Requires the exact initiating browser cookie session; bearer-only transport is refused.

post.summary: Create a browser-cookie or native-bearer session
post.description: Browser callers omit `client` and receive an HTTP-only session cookie. Native callers send `client: native` and receive `sessionToken`. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; the native login envelope may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Delete the active session when present
post.description: The operation is idempotent and succeeds even when no valid session exists. It clears the browser session cookie and deletes the authenticated bearer or cookie session when present. It does not revoke the owner's durable agent connection. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Read the current optional session

put.description: The authenticated owner grants one explicit, versioned agent-tool catalog. Replaying the same catalog is idempotent and preserves its connection timestamp; choosing a newer catalog is an explicit upgrade and records a new connection timestamp. The durable grant survives page reloads, browser restarts, logout, and session expiry until the owner explicitly disconnects it. Omitting the request body retains the historical v1 behavior. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

delete.description: The authenticated owner explicitly revokes the durable agent connection. The mutation is idempotent. Logging out or deleting an application session does not perform this operation. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Upload one image, video, or document to an owned link
post.description: The multipart field name is `file`. One file of at most 25 MiB is accepted, with at most eight media records per link. Supported MIME types are image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, video/mp4, video/webm, and video/quicktime. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers. Document types include PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, CSV, Markdown, and JSON. Known extensions may resolve an empty or generic browser MIME; arbitrary binary and active HTML/script types are rejected. Attachments retain media IDs, owner privacy, the shared eight-file limit, and Undo.

get.summary: List top-level Life Links or one owned Life Link's immediate children
get.description: Omit `parentId` to list top-level Life Links. Supply an owned `parentId` to list only its immediate children. Results sort by normalized title, creation time, then stable ID and page with an opaque cursor; the endpoint never recursively returns the whole hierarchy.

post.summary: Create a private top-level or child Life Link
post.description: Creates one Life Link with an optional stable caller ID, item/container browsing role, structured context and public-field selection. Defaults are item, private, schemaVersion 1 context and no public fields. Matching stable-ID create retries converge; changed payloads conflict. A parent must belong to the owner and parented creation confirms placement. Adding the first child promotes an item parent to container. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Search the authenticated owner's Life Links
get.description: Performs bounded, owner-scoped search across title, compatibility body text, recorded ancestor path, and QR identity. Match classes rank exact QR, exact or prefix title, title, recorded path, then body; results within a class sort by normalized title, updatedAt descending, then stable ID. Each result includes bounded path and body context plus explicit truncation and continuation metadata.

get.summary: Read one owned Life Link with bounded hierarchy context
get.description: Returns the exact canonical Life Link, bounded ancestry, immediate children and an initial Collection-membership page. The cursor/limit query applies to children; continue memberships through the dedicated collection-memberships route. Every returned membership includes all its assigned Sections. Explicit continuation metadata prevents partial pages from implying complete absence. No public QR response exposes hierarchy or membership.

patch.summary: Update one owned Life Link's content or privacy
patch.description: Requires the exact `expectedUpdatedAt` revision returned by a prior owner read. Stale writes fail with `409 stale_life_link`; the server never silently overwrites newer canonical owner state. Supports title/body, privacy, full structured-context replacement and exact public-field selection. Omitted context preserves existing values. Browsing role, placement, and QR binding are not accepted here. The page-bound content tool uses title/body/context; explicit public-projection maintenance uses privacy/publicFieldKeys through its own discriminated tool action. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

patch.summary: Replace one owned Life Link's parent or detach it to the top level
patch.description: Set `parentId` to an owned Life Link or null to detach. The operation requires `expectedUpdatedAt`, changes only the selected node's parent edge, and rejects stale revisions, self-parenting, cycles, missing parents, and cross-owner placement with structured conflicts. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Upload one image, video, or document to any owned Life Link
post.description: The multipart field name is `file`. One file of at most 25 MiB is accepted, with at most eight media records per Life Link. Supported MIME types are image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, video/mp4, video/webm, and video/quicktime. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers. Document types include PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, CSV, Markdown, and JSON. Known extensions may resolve an empty or generic browser MIME; arbitrary binary and active HTML/script types are rejected. Attachments retain media IDs, owner privacy, the shared eight-file limit, and Undo.

get.summary: Read media from one owned Life Link
get.description: This canonical route is owner-only, including for public Life Links. Media bytes are not included in the public-field allowlist; QR-keyed media also requires the owner.

delete.summary: Delete media from one owned Life Link
delete.description: Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Create and persist a batch of unclaimed QR links
post.description: Supported callers send an integer count from 1 through 10000. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Download a batch mapping as CSV
Download a batch mapping and SVG QR images as ZIP
Resolve the viewer-filtered state of a QR link
get.description: Authentication is optional. Owners receive their private content; other viewers receive the public, private-placeholder, unclaimed, or not-found state. Non-owner claimed responses force ownerId to null and media to an empty array. Body and bodyDoc are empty unless notes is explicitly selected; context contains only selected summary/condition/experience/plan values. They never expose canonical Life Link identity, parent, ancestry, children, path, root, descendant, hierarchy fields, placement, Collection membership, or Section assignments.

post.summary: Idempotently claim a QR or attach it to an eligible owned Life Link
post.description: `commandId` in the JSON body and `Idempotency-Key` in the header are two bindings for the same command identity; when both are present, the non-empty body value takes precedence. Replaying the same command identity for the same effective owner and QR returns the recorded claim result with the current authorized QR state. Reusing it for a different owner or QR returns `idempotency_key_conflict`. Create-and-bind remains the default when `mode` is omitted; explicit `mode: attach` requires `lifeLinkId` and binds only an eligible existing untagged Life Link owned by the caller. Replay/conflict comparison also binds the mode and requested target. If neither command binding is supplied, the server generates an identity. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

post.summary: Compare a scanned QR value with a target QR identifier
post.description: The scan value may be a Life Links QR URL or a bare Life Links QR identifier. Browser-origin enforcement applies to browser mutations; authenticated native bearer calls may omit browser Origin and Referer headers.

get.summary: Open the stable browser page for a QR link
get.description: Returns the Life Links browser application shell. The browser application resolves viewer-filtered QR state through `GET /api/qr/{qrId}`. After the configured challenge-host cutover, HTML navigation on the explicitly retained Railway hostname redirects to the canonical HTTPS origin with the same path and query. QR identity, API behavior and viewer filtering remain unchanged; browser sessions remain host-only.

307.description: Temporary, non-cached browser navigation redirect from the explicitly retained challenge hostname to https://lifelinks.vmosaic.com. API and asset requests are not redirected.

Location.description: Canonical HTTPS origin with the original browser path and query.

get.summary: Describe or render an exact owned attachment page or frame
get.description: Owner-authenticated derived image delivery from canonical bytes. Describe returns byte/MIME SHA-256 sourceRevision; overview/crop require it. Static images use oriented original pixels. PDF/DOCX/XLSX use one-based page (default 1) and a rotated 288-DPI grid in source.pdf/source.office. Office is a nonexecuting cached-value print projection: stored formula/field/chart display, no recalculation/external refresh; warnings disclose conversion/hidden/print limitations. Animation uses one-based frame (default 1), composited pixels and declared frame timing/count/loops. Video uses atMs (default 0); source.video identifies actual decoded presentation time/PTS. Selectors are mutually exclusive and repeated for describe/overview/crop. Other pages, frames, audio, hidden content and embedded files are not inspected. No OCR transcript or whole-file comprehension claim. Bounds: 512 pages or animation frames, five-minute videos, eight streams, 25 MiB source, 32 million pixels/16384 edge, 2048 output edge/2 MiB PNG or JPEG. No upscaling. Overview can reduce further with warnings; crop never silently reduces for byte cap. Shared two-unit/eight-queued admission: ordinary JS reads cost one/15 seconds, native Office/temporal reads cost both/90 seconds. Parent-owned process-tree cancellation and temporary cleanup; qualified native runtime is Linux, missing/unsupported runtime returns runtime_unavailable. No OS sandbox, persistent derivative, public URL, external provider upload or model-seen claim. Authorization/session/source are rechecked before release. Invalid selectors/regions return 400; malformed/encrypted/resource limits are explicit unreadable results.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Describe source metadata; render overview or exact crop.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: PDF/DOCX/XLSX one-based page, default 1. Exclusive with frame/atMs. Repeat for overview/crop.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.description: Animation-only one-based frame, default 1; exclusive with page/atMs.

parameters.name: atMs
parameters.description: Video-only requested time in milliseconds, default zero; actual decoded time is returned. Exclusive with page/frame.

parameters.name: sourceRevision
parameters.description: Required for overview/crop; forbidden for describe.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Required only for crop; integer oriented-image pixels or rotated PDF page-grid pixels at source.pdf.pixelsPerPoint.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Required only for crop; integer oriented-image pixels or rotated PDF page-grid pixels at source.pdf.pixelsPerPoint.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Required only for crop; integer oriented-image pixels or rotated PDF page-grid pixels at source.pdf.pixelsPerPoint.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Required only for crop; integer oriented-image pixels or rotated PDF page-grid pixels at source.pdf.pixelsPerPoint.

parameters.name: maxEdge
parameters.description: Optional overview/crop maximum output edge; no upscaling.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: Optional overview/crop encoding; explicit JPEG is lossy.

200.description: Private source description, bounded encoded image, or explicit unreadable reason. Image bytes do not establish model-facing delivery.

409.description: Source revision, exact source bytes or MIME changed; no substituted image.

get.summary: Read paginated extracted text or an explicit video speech window
get.description: Owner-authenticated, read-only derived text from canonical attachment bytes. Default extraction supports PDF, DOCX, XLSX and UTF-8 TXT/CSV/Markdown/JSON; images/video and encrypted/scanned/malformed or resource-limited documents return explicit unreadable results. DOCX includes source-labelled body, related headers/footers, footnotes/endnotes and comments with IDs/reference markers; orphan ZIP parts are excluded. Ready means pageable extracted text, not complete visual interpretation. Explicit representation=transcript instead selects a video-audio window (startMs default 0, durationMs default 30000, maximum 30000) and optional global audioStreamIndex; local pinned whisper.cpp/base recognition is inferred, never owner-reported or a complete audiovisual interpretation. Transcript metadata identifies actual window end, source duration, stream, processor/model hash and nextStartMs; nextOffset pages text within that same window. Five-minute/eight-stream source bounds and a 150-second native job deadline apply. Offsets count UTF-16 code units and never split surrogate pairs. Continuations require the returned revision (bytes/MIME/extraction version, plus requested window/stream/model for speech). DOCX retains life-links-attachment-text-docx-v2. No summaries, external provider uploads, document execution or DB writes. Default extraction bounds: 15-second job, 128 MiB V8 heap, 2048 ZIP entries, 64 MiB total/16 MiB individual inflated bytes, 8 MiB extracted UTF-8 text, 512 PDF pages, 128 sheets and 100000 populated cells. Shared two-unit/eight-queued admission: ordinary reads cost one, native jobs both. Output-limit failure never returns successful partial content. Owner/session/source are rechecked before release; missing/unsupported native runtime returns runtime_unavailable.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

BrowserOrigin.name: Origin
BrowserOrigin.description: Required by deployment policy for browser mutations unless a same-origin Referer is available. Authenticated native bearer calls, and native login requests, may omit browser-origin headers.

CalendarStartDate.name: startDate
CalendarStartDate.description: Inclusive local-date lower bound. Must be supplied with endDate; the window may span at most 366 days.

CalendarEndDate.name: endDate
CalendarEndDate.description: Inclusive local-date upper bound. Must be supplied with startDate; the window may span at most 366 days.

RequestId.description: Request correlation identifier accepted from a valid X-Request-Id request header or generated by the server. Values in the service's native session-token lexical space are rejected and replaced with a generated identifier so credentials cannot enter logs through this header.

RetryAfter.description: Whole seconds until the active rate-limit bucket resets.

SessionCookie.description: Browser session cookie. Login sets it only when `client: native` is absent; logout clears it.

ContentDisposition.description: Inline media filename or attachment download filename.

CacheControl.description: Owner media uses `private, no-store`; media is never served as a public field.

authorizationUrl.description: Opaque Microsoft authorization URL. Navigate in the initiating authenticated browser; do not log or share it.

Not an identity, ownership or permission key; providerAccountId remains authoritative. The last known same-account label may be retained when optional metadata is unavailable; disconnected legacy records can omit it.

timeZone.description: Normalized provider-supplied IANA time zone. Omitted when the provider exposes none; never inferred from an event.

CalendarProviderSelectionRequest.description: Owner-only selection of exact discovered calendars. When agentAccessByCalendarId is supplied its keys must exactly match selectedCalendarIds and each access choice must fit freshly discovered provider capabilities. Omission defaults new/reconnected calendars to none and preserves existing settings during additional selection. Authorization retries bind IDs and access choices; completed retries never reapply grants. Additional selection cannot change an already connected calendar's grant; use its revision-checked settings route instead.

CalendarProviderAvailability.description: Truthful runtime configuration, not proof an account is connected. Google authorization remains unavailable.

build_sha.description: Deployed build identity. APP_ENV=webmcp-challenge requires the nonzero full lowercase 40-hex submitted public Git commit SHA.

canonical_source_sha.description: Canonical source identity. APP_ENV=webmcp-challenge requires the nonzero full lowercase 40-hex private canonical Git commit SHA mapped to the public release.

source_tree_sha256.description: Normalized tracked release-allowlist digest. APP_ENV=webmcp-challenge requires a nonzero lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 value.

competition_fixture_profile.description: Competition fixture implemented by this binary. The fixed reset operator requires this successor profile in addition to exact qualified release identity before mutation.

ownerId.description: Owner identity for owner-authorized responses; null in non-owner public QR projections.

context.description: Owner context, or only explicitly selected public context values for a non-owner. Public projections omit unselected values, ancestry, placement, membership, and media.

ownerId.description: Owner identity for an authorized owner projection; null in a non-owner public claimed projection.

bodyDoc.description: The serialized JSON document is limited to 128 KiB and nesting is normalized to at most 16 levels.
